Key sentence: “With inflation running persistently below this longer-run goal, the Committee will aim to achieve inflation moderately above 2 percent for some time …” balanced against “The ongoing public health crisis will continue to weigh on economic activity, employment, and inflation … and poses considerable risks to the economic outlook.”

Why the adjustment using the literature:
- The shift to average inflation targeting (AIT) announced by Chair Powell at the 2020 Jackson Hole symposium implies a make-up strategy that should raise inflation expectations and lower real rates when at the zero lower bound, a dovish signal consistent with the Committee’s stated intent to let inflation moderately exceed 2% (Federal Reserve adopts make-up strategy; Jay Powell shift toward AIT). This tempers the purely negative tone.
- At the zero lower bound, the literature supports using forward guidance and quantitative easing to provide accommodation (Federal Reserve utilizes forward guidance; utilizes quantitative easing; concerned about zero lower bound). The statement’s commitment to keep the funds rate at 0–0.25% and continue Treasury/MBS purchases aligns with that playbook (Bernanke and related work on ZLB tools), improving the risk outlook relative to no action.
- Clarida’s work on the Taylor principle implies policy should respond strongly to inflation shortfalls. The Committee’s explicit promise to overshoot after persistent undershooting is consistent with that guidance, supporting better-anchored expectations.
- Continued purchases of Treasuries and agency MBS support smooth market functioning and credit transmission through the term premium and housing channels (Federal Reserve buys MBS; influences money supply), which the literature associates with easier financial conditions.
- Nonetheless, the pandemic materially raises economic policy uncertainty and downside risks (COVID-19 pandemic increases economic policy uncertainty), justifying a tone that remains slightly negative overall.

Net: strong accommodation and credible AIT-forward guidance tilt the tone toward neutral, but prominent pandemic-related risks keep it modestly negative.
